newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates slip, zero coupon bonds rally.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates slip, zero coupon bonds rally.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday around 10.00-10.25 percent and most of the deals were at 10.60 percent level, dealers said.
"Almost everyone has covered themselves on the eve of the reporting Friday," a dealer at a foreign bank said.

Prices of government securities were unchanged, dealers said. The zero coupon bonds saw some speculative interest with zero coupon bond maturing in 2000 quoted at 59.75 rupees, up from the Wednesday's level of 59.57 rupees.
The zero coupon bond maturing in 1999 rose to 73.13 rupees. The yield on these zero coupon bonds at 14 percent was very attractive, a dealer said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded on Thursday at 13 percent and the 13.62 percent stock was traded at 13.47 percent while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 13.37 percent, dealers said.
The total volume traded in the market was 920 million against the Wednesday's volume of 1800 million, a dealer on the National Stock Exchange said.
He said there was no activity in certificates of deposit (CDs) and commercial paper, but public sector bonds attracted some buying interest.
Intercorporate deposits were steady in the 17-19 percent range for top-rated companies, dealers said.
